title: `Auth.setAuthority` Reverts for Owner When `authority` Is Zero — Permanently Freezes Authority Rotation
impact: The guard is `require(msg.sender == owner || authority.canCall(...))`. Solidity evaluates `||` left-to-right and short-circuits, so if `msg.sender == owner` the second clause is skipped — **but only if the owner check passes first**. The real hazard is the inverse: if `authority` is initialized to `address(0)` (a common deployment pattern) and the *owner* is not `msg.sender` at that moment (e.g., ownership was transferred to a multisig that later delegates, or an integrator constructs with `address(0)` authority expecting to set it later), the expression `authority.canCall(...)` performs an external call on `address(0)`. High-level calls to `address(0)` revert in Solidity ≥0.8, bricking `setAuthority` for any non-owner caller. More critically, **if `owner` is ever set to a contract that cannot call (e.g., a non-forwarding multisig or an EOA that lost keys) while `authority` is zero, authority can never be updated**, permanently freezing all `requiresAuth` functions that depend on authority-based authorization.
